sentences.text: Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 03rd January, 2012 passed in Motor Accident Claims Petition No.659 of 2008 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Petition (Main), Rakot, the original opponent No.2 - insurance company has preferred this First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No.659 of 2008
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1079/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 1.1
The original claim of the claimants was for Rs.04,84,500/-.
As against that, learned Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.02,34,900/- with 9% interest.
2. It is the claim of the claimants that on 10 th December, 2007 the deceased was travelling in mini bus bearing Registration No.GJ-3W-5472 with moderate speed on correct side.
However, the bus turned turtle, in which the deceased sustained serious injuries and ultimately succumbed to those injuries.
2.1 Therefore, the claimants being heirs and legal representatives of the deceased approached the learned Tribunal seeking compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

3. The Tribunal, after having considered the material on record, awarded sum of Rs.02,34,900/-
with 9% interest.
4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid, the insurance company has approached this Court by way of this Appeal disputing their liability to satisfy the claim.
5. I have heard learned advocate Ms.Lilu Bhaya for the appellant - insurance company and learned advocate Mr.Hemal Shah for the claimants.

6. Learned advocate for the insurance company has raised the sole contention that the claim under Section 163A is no-fault liability and therefore, the same can be defeated by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1079/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined the insurance company by proving that the deceased was at fault or negligent for the accident in question.

To substantiate her contention, learned advocate for the insurance company place reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Ningamma & Anr. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2009) 13 SCC 710].
6.1

entities.text: Ningamma & Anr. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. [(2009) 13 SCC 710]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By making above submission, learned advocate has prayed this Court to allow the Appeal in the interest of justice.

7. Per contra, learned advocate Mr.Hemal Shah for the claimants has vehemently opposed the present Appeal contending that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is just and legal and no interference is called for.

Learned advocate further submitted that the contention raised by learned advocate for the appellant is now squarely covered in favour of the claimants in the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar [2018 (1)
GLH 1].

By making above submission, learned advocate for the claimants has prayed this Court to dismiss the Appeal.
8. I have heard learned advocates for the respective parties and have gone through the record and proceedings of the learned Tribunal.
No other and/or further submissions have been canvassed by learned advocates appearing for the respective parties except what are stated hereinabove.

9. Considering the submissions of rival parties, the short question that falls for consideration of this Court is whether in a claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1079/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined Vehicles Act is it open for the insurer to raise defense or plea of negligence?
10. The aforesaid question is no more res integra.
The Apex Court, in the case of Sunil Kumar (supra), has decided the question as under.

"From the above discussion, it is clear that grant of compensation under Section 163-A of the Act on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of a final award and the adjudication thereunder is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle(s) involved in the accident.
This is made explicit by Section 163A(2).

Though the aforesaid section of the Act does not specifically exclude a possible defence of the Insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated by Section 140(4), to permit such defence to be introduced by the Insurer and/or to understand the provisions of Section 163-A of the Act to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of Section 163-A of the Act, namely,
final compensation within a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situations where the claims of compensation on the basis of fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

In fact, to understand Section 163-A of the Act to permit the Insurer to raise the defence of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under Section 163-A of the Act at par with the proceeding under Section 166 of the Act which would not only be self-contradictory but also defeat the very legislative intention."
(Para 8)

"For the aforesaid reasons, we answer the question arising by holding that in a proceeding under Section 163-A of the Act it is not open for the Insurer to raise any defence of negligence on the part of the victim."

(Para 9)
11.

It is pertinent to note that while deciding the aforesaid question, the Apex Court has also considered the earlier judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Sinitha [(2012) 2 SCC 356] and overruled the said judgment by the decision of Sunil Kumar (supra).
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1079/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, the present Appeal is bereft of any merits and is accordingly dismissed.
